searchText: Yes, this is fixed in the storage layout that is currently being proposed for verkle tries. Pardon my ignorance, but by *flat* I meant address being key, and encoded account representation as value. No trie. Data retrieved from the network has to be "provable" meaning it needs an accompanying proof that anchors it to a known state root. <@329594653097721856> everything cleared up or am I misunderstanding your question? for now yes, thank you! one more thing though: I know it's better to build iteratively, but have you thought about incentivization? (although it's not strictly related to DHT iself - more about billing integration - e.g. whitelisting node ids / ENRs) Yes, and explicitly chose against it. LES is already going in the direction of incentives. I'm of the opinion that they A: aren't required and B: can end up introducing perverse incentives so we expect people to share state out of pure altruism?... Correct Altruism and laziness. 😄 It turns out, most people run whatever software you write as-is, so if you write something that shares, people will share. Never underestimate the power of laziness and software defaults
